assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapy is a clear chain from basic peptide biology to drugs that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with growing evidence in cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional, and the neuroendocrine appetite-regulation angle is of direct interest to a neuropharmacologist.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its incretin action) and Drucker (proglucagon biology, GLP-1/GLP-2 actions, translation) are the core basic-science contributors. Knudsen is decisive for the long-acting analogues that made the therapy work. Mojsov's early peptide characterisation is also important and credit among her, Habener and others is contested, so a three-person limit leaves a difficult omission.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy and safety are confirmed by large independent phase 3 and outcome trials over more than a decade, and the field is at peak visibility, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: How to weigh the early GLP-1 sequence and peptide work (Mojsov and others) against physiology and drug development.
Whether the committee wishes to credit an industry scientist alongside academic discoverers.
Long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells for cancer opened a new therapeutic modality, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemia and lymphoma and expansion to myeloma and possibly autoimmune disease. The concept is original, the clinical impact is clear and it has had lasting influence on immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered TIL/TCR work) give a reasonable three-person set. Other pioneers, such as Eshhar and Kuwana for the original chimeric receptor concept, are not in the supplied credit list and I cannot assess them here.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up. Toxicity, manufacturing cost and limited efficacy in solid tumours are open, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: The boundary between concept, receptor design and clinical translation could be argued differently.
Rosenberg's inclusion depends on how broadly adoptive cell therapy is treated.
Efficacy in solid tumours is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience a tool for causal, cell-type-specific control of neural circuits and has reshaped systems neuroscience and begun to influence therapy for blindness. The channelrhodopsin discovery was original and the tool is used across most of neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Hegemann and Nagel (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth, with Boyden, established neuronal use, and Miesenboeck contributed early genetically targeted photostimulation. Six credited names cannot fit within three, so any choice leaves out decisive contributors. This is the main attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for about two decades. Its impact is as a tool rather than as a therapy, which some would consider a weaker fit with the physiology or medicine remit, although therapeutic extensions are emerging.
uncertainties: Allocation among Boyden, Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg and Miesenboeck is unresolved and contentious.
Clinical translation is still early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a largely manageable one, and established the proof of concept for oncogene-directed therapy. Clarity of discovery and durable impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound programme), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Lasker recognition already exists. The BCR-ABL fusion discoveries belong to other prizewinners and others, which could complicate the narrative.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of survival data and independent confirmation. Fully mature, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether an industry chemist is credited alongside clinicians.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from previously recognised cancer genetics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing TNF as a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis led to the anti-TNF class and to a general principle of cytokine blockade in chronic inflammatory disease. The impact is large across rheumatology, gastroenterology and dermatology.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly identified TNF as the dominant driver in RA synovium and led the clinical proof-of-concept, so the pairing is natural. Contributions in cytokine biology and antibody engineering (for example by Vilcek and others) are outside the supplied credit and could be argued to matter.
assessment.maturity: Long-established clinical use with extensive independent confirmation. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether the credit omits antibody-engineering or TNF-biology contributors.
Recent immunology prizes may reduce appetite for another immunology award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying alpha-synuclein as the main component of Lewy bodies and neurites, and tau in neurodegenerative filaments, defined the molecular pathology of Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies and tauopathies. It underpins current biomarker work such as seed-amplification assays and imaging tracers, and is of high interest from a clinical neurology point of view. I recognise that my own field makes me want to apply stricter scrutiny.
assessment.attribution: Spillantini and Goedert are the clear shared authors of the key alpha-synuclein and tau filament findings. The earlier genetic link between SNCA mutations and PD was established by others and is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed as pathology and diagnostic tool, and cryo-EM filament structures extend it. Disease-modifying therapy based on it has not been shown to work, so the clinical translation is incomplete.
uncertainties: No validated disease-modifying therapy yet.
The causal role of aggregates, as opposed to marker status, is still debated.
Genetic contributions to alpha-synuclein biology are not part of this credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, an effective treatment for spinal muscular atrophy and an influential model for splice-switching therapeutics. The mechanism is clear and the patient benefit is striking, particularly with early treatment.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's splicing-regulation work and Bennett's antisense chemistry and drug development are the central contributions. Others, such as Hua and Krainer in the SMN2 ASO work, and groups on SMN gene identification, may need consideration. Two names are a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up, and the approach is replicated by other RNA-based therapies. Recognition is plausible, although the platform is still maturing.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier RNA prizes may affect reception.
Long-term outcomes across age groups are still emerging.
Contribution of other SMN-targeting groups is outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signalling pathway from ER to nucleus, revealed a basic principle of cellular quality control with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and jointly defined the Ire1/HAC1 (XBP1) signalling in yeast and the pathway logic, with Walter's laboratory also establishing Ire1 splicing mechanism. Pairing is clean. Mammalian contributions (for example Ron, Harding) lie outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of confirmation, with clinical relevance still being tested, e.g. ISR modulators. The fundamental discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation is limited so far.
Role of the integrated stress response and mammalian PERK/ATF6 work is outside this credit.
